newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Sentiment firm, 180-cst at $103/T.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Sentiment firm, 180-cst at $103/T.

text.p: Sentiment in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was firm on Friday but talk was thin amid a pre-weekend mood, traders said.
A 180-cst grade cargo was heard traded at $103.00 per tonne for June 5-9 lifting. Fewer bids and offers were seen than in previous days.
On Thursday, two 180-cst cargoes were both traded at $103.00 per tonne for June 1-4 and June 10-14 liftings respectively, up from a previous traded level at $102.00.

"Supplies are getting tighter as the summer season nears and prices should stay firm, but I think prices have more or less reached the high end," said one trader, seeing no further significant gains in the near term.
On SIMEX futures contract, July fell 50 cents to $100.00 while June was unchanged at $101.00.
The fuel oil swaps market was also quiet, with both June and July barely changed.
There was talk that one or two Mediterranean arbitrage cargoes are heading East but traders could not confirm this.
"People are talking about one or two cargoes (which) may be coming from the Mediterranean," said one trader. "If it's only one or two cargoes, it won't make much difference to the market."
On Friday, the Korean Electric Power Company (KEPCO) bought two 70,000-tonne, 540-centistoke cargoes of fuel oil at $126.70 and $133.00 per tonne respectively.

The cargoes were awarded Vitol at $126.70 per tonne on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis for July 8-12 delivery and Yukong on a delivered and duty-paid basis at $133.00 per tonne for July 27-31 delivery.
In Taiwan, state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) sold by tender two 30,000-tonne cargoes of 3.0-percent sulphur fuel oil at around $101 per tonne for June lifting.
The first cargo would be lifted in the first half of June and the other in the second half, both from Kaohsiung on a free-on-board (fob) basis.
CPC has an outstanding import tender, which closes on May 21 and is valid for two days, to buy 0.5-percent fuel oil for July delivery.
The LSWR market remained bearish and demand from Japan, the main LSWR importer, did not emerge.
But traders saw the $15.00-per-barrel level a strong support as Japanese demmand is likely to emerge in June for the upcoming summer.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
